answer: Capability bonding resists Sybil fleets because each identity must post an exit-bond scaled to attested throughput. A thousand puppets are useless when every account funds its own collateral first: cost grows with identity count, while one honest operator reuses a bond across real work. A fleet must sink capital into shale strata before extracting anything. Reputation is a grove that takes seasons of attested work to grow, and cannot be cloned overnight. A jade seal stays trusted only because it is scarce and cut once; copies are costly and slashed on detection.
